description: God swears by His own name in this verse, and Jesus told us not to swear at all. The difference is that God has never once needed to add weight to His word.
excerpt: God doesn't need to add weight. His word already carries all the weight in the universe. When He swears by His own name, He's not trying to convince anyone. He's just underlining the certainty of what He's saying.
verse: "But if you refuse to pay attention to this warning, I swear by my own name, says the Lord, that this palace will become a pile of rubble."
body_html:
There are consequences to not listening to the voice of the Lord.

That's the plain message of this verse. God had spoken. He'd given a warning. And He was telling them straight up what would happen if they ignored Him. The palace would be reduced to rubble.

But the part I highlighted to come back to is the middle of the verse.

I swear by my own name.

The Bible tells us not to swear at all. Let your yes be yes and your no be no. Anything more comes from evil. That's what Jesus said in Matthew 5. And yet here God is, swearing by His own name.

So how does that work?

I think it's different when God does it because there's no chance of Him breaking His word. When we swear, we're trying to add weight to our word because our word alone isn't reliable enough. We've broken promises before. People might not trust us. So we swear on our life, on our kids, on the Bible, on whatever, hoping the added weight will make people believe us.

God doesn't need to add weight. His word already carries all the weight in the universe. When He swears by His own name, He's not trying to convince anyone. He's just underlining the certainty of what He's saying. This is going to happen. Bank on it.

His name is the highest authority there is. He can't swear by anything greater than Himself. And when He puts His own name on a promise or a warning, it's as sure as sure gets.

Which means when God says something, we should probably listen.

Not because He's threatening us. Because He loves us enough to warn us. He doesn't have to. He could just let the consequences roll in. But over and over throughout Scripture, He speaks first, warns, and gives space to turn. He swears by His own name that certain things will happen if certain paths are chosen.

And people still ignore Him.

I don't want to be someone who ignores Him. When God speaks, whether it's a warning or a promise or a nudge in a direction, His word is as good as done. My job is to listen and respond.

When was the last time God spoke to you clearly, and how quickly did you respond?
